page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, paired with 31.0 GB of system memory. The instance includes a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, providing 16 GB of VRAM. It has no local storage and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split. General CPU compute metrics are low, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance falling into the bottom 25 percent, and Geekbench single-core scores in the bottom 10 percent. However, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong acceleration for specific workloads. Large-block memory bandwidth is average, and LLM inference speeds are highly competitive, reaching the top 10 percent for prompt processing on both 135M and 7B models, and the top 25 percent for 7B model text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server trades off raw CPU performance for GPU-accelerated capabilities. It is positioned as an entry point for GPU workloads rather than a high-compute CPU instance. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment. The hardware profile is best suited for low-intensity machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, and GPU-accelerated video or image processing rather than heavy general-purpose database operations or CPU-bound compilation tasks.

Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps and contains no local storage. Benchmark results indicate weak general CPU and memory performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores placing in the bottom 25 percent. Conversely, the server excels in GPU-driven tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing for 135M and 7B models. This hardware profile represents a qualitative tradeoff, offering cost-efficient GPU acceleration for machine learning inference and media processing at the expense of raw CPU compute power.
